title: Scaled dot-product attention: scores
narration: Let's compute the first half of scaled dot-product attention. The paper writes it as softmax of Q times K transpose over the square root of d k, times V. [[c_q]]Here is a tiny query matrix Q with two queries, each of length four, so d k is four. [[c_k]]Next is the key matrix K, with two keys, also of length four. [[c_row]]To score a query against a key, we take their dot product. Look at the first query and the second key. Multiply matching entries: two times zero, zero times one, two times zero, zero times one. That adds up to zero. [[c_s]]Doing this for every query and key pair is exactly Q times K transpose, and gives this two by two score matrix. The second query scores two with the first key, and four with the second key, so it matches the second key best. [[c_div]]Now we divide every score by the square root of d k. Since d k is four, that is divide by two. [[c_out]]The scaled scores are one, zero, one and two. This scaling stops the dot products growing too large when d k is big, which would push the softmax into regions with tiny gradients. Next, we will turn these scores into weights.

objects.text: d_k = 4, so the square root of d_k is 2
